item.title: Companies Rush to Close Daring Deals Under Trump
item.description: Companies are seizing on what many say is perhaps the most favorable regulatory environment for businesses in years.
item.dc:creator: Lauren Hirsch
item.media:description: NextEra Energy, led by John Ketchum, its chief executive, and Dominion Energy announced their merger in May.

item.title: Inflation Worries Prompted Fed Officials to Dissent on Holding Rates Steady
item.description: Internal divisions over whether to raise interest rates intensified at Kevin Warsh’s second meeting as chairman of the Federal Reserve.
item.dc:creator: Colby Smith
item.category: US and Israeli Attack on Iran (2026)
item.media:description: Disagreement inside the Federal Reserve has materialized early in Kevin M. Warsh’s tenure as chairman.

item.title: South Korea’s KOSPI Soars 18%
item.description: South Korea’s KOSPI index has swung wildly because of both the enthusiasm and anxiety related to investing in the global artificial intelligence boom.
item.dc:creator: Choe Sang-Hun
item.media:description: South Korea’s benchmark index has whipsawed in recent days, surging a record 18 percent on Friday.

item.title: Todd Blanche’s Loyalty to Trump Is Putting His Attorney General Confirmation at Risk
item.description: Todd Blanche’s approach has collided with the jury-of-two reality in the Senate that has, thus far, kept him from the prize he covets: the stability and status conferred by a Senate confirmation.
item.dc:creator: Glenn Thrush
item.media:description: Todd Blanche, according to current and former officials, understands that coping with President Trump’s demands, rages and U-turns is the price to pay for rising in his orbit.

item.title: Trump to Appeal Judge’s Ruling Denouncing I.R.S. Lawsuit as Exercise in Self-Dealing
item.description: It was the latest sign that the president was doubling down on his fight for aspects of a deal that brings him vast benefits, even though they have jeopardized the confirmation of his pick for attorney general.
item.dc:creator: Alan Feuer and Andrew Duehren
item.media:description: President Trump reiterated his support for the so-called anti-weaponization fund in a social media post on Friday.

item.title: Amid Talk of a Party Switch, Fetterman Vows ‘Never’
item.description: Changing one’s affiliation is rare in the Senate, but it can have big consequences. John Fetterman of Pennsylvania says he is staying put as a Democrat.
item.dc:creator: Carl Hulse
item.media:description: Senator John Fetterman, Democrat of Pennsylvania, at the Capitol this week.

item.title: How the Pro-Trump Media Ecosystem Is Splintering Ahead of the Midterms
item.description: Once united in support of President Trump, right-wing influencers are embroiled in feuds and losing viewers, creating a problem for Republicans in the midterm elections.
item.dc:creator: Stuart A. Thompson

item.title: Trump’s Gaza Deal Sparks Questions on Whether Israel and Hamas Will Comply
item.description: The new 15-point plan, released by the Board of Peace and announced by Trump, calls in part for Israel to end its attacks and Hamas to give up its weapons.
item.dc:creator: Adam Rasgon
item.media:credit: Saher Alghorra for The New York Times
item.media:description: Palestinians inspecting the site of a strike in Gaza City on Thursday.

item.title: I Flew in the Douglas DC-3, a WWII Workhorse of Aviation, Over the Amazon
item.description: The Douglas DC-3 was mass-produced during World War II. Today, one of the few still remaining transports passengers in Colombia’s jungle.
item.dc:creator: Max Bearak and Federico Rios
item.media:credit: Federico Rios Escobar for The New York Times

item.title: What Caused the Surge of Migrants From Morocco Into Ceuta?
item.description: Speculation has focused on lax Moroccan policing, attractive Spanish immigration policies and misinformation from human traffickers. In reality, experts said, it’s too early to know.
item.dc:creator: Jonathan Wolfe
item.media:description: A Spanish soldier keeping watch on Friday at the Spanish-Moroccan border.

item.title: Ukraine’s Strike on Iranian Ship Shows How Two Wars Could Spiral
item.description: Iran sent military aid to Russia for its war against Ukraine. Now the question is whether that conflict and the U.S.-Israeli war against Iran are converging.
item.dc:creator: Edward Wong
item.category: US and Israeli Attack on Iran (2026)
item.media:description: President Volodymyr Zelensky of Ukraine at the U.S. Capitol on Tuesday. Mr. Zelensky has tried to make the case that the wars in the Middle East and in Ukraine have some common elements.

item.title: Emily Wilson’s Pan of ‘The Odyssey’ Ignites a Debate Among Classicists and Commenters
item.description: Wilson, whose 2017 translation of Homer’s Greek classic influenced the director Christopher Nolan, panned his screenplay for the movie version in an essay for The London Review of Books.
item.dc:creator: Neil Vigdor
item.media:credit: Trustees of the University of Pennsylvania

item.title: Adam O’Neal Resigns as Washington Post Opinion Editor
item.description: Adam O’Neal inherited a mandate from the paper’s owner, Jeff Bezos, to shift toward “personal liberties and free markets.”
item.dc:creator: Erik Wemple
item.media:credit: Michael A. McCoy for The New York Times

item.title: Coast Guard Vows to Protect Crews From Brain Injuries Caused by Rough Seas

item.description: Untreated and undiagnosed, the crews that save lives in the roughest seas face the relentless pounding of waves.

item.category: United States Defense and Military Forces

item.title: Plug-In Solar Panels Are Starting to Sprout in U.S. Backyards
item.description: Ten U.S. states have legalized systems that can be plugged into standard wall outlets. The technology typically does not require permits or electricians.
item.dc:creator: Ivan Penn and Claire Brown
item.media:credit: Poppy Lynch for The New York Times
item.media:description: Alex Ottoboni with his balcony solar panel at his condo in the San Francisco Bay Area

item.title: What You Need to Know About Installing Plug-In Solar Panels
item.description: You can now buy panels that plug into electrical outlets, but there are some important safety issues to consider when picking and installing a system.
item.dc:creator: Ivan Penn and Claire Brown
item.media:credit: Patrick Junker for The New York Times
item.media:description: Plug-in solar panels are as large as windows, and in Germany they are often installed on balconies.

item.title: Military Testosterone Policy Raises Questions About Its Links to Aggression
item.description: A new policy raises questions about testosterone’s effect on aggression in some men.
item.dc:creator: Azeen Ghorayshi
item.category: United States Defense and Military Forces
item.media:description: Recent evidence points to a condition called “operator syndrome,” a pattern of medical problems, including decreased testosterone, that those who have served long stretches in special operations units are more likely to report.

item.title: G.O.P. Kills Bid to Expand I.V.F. Access in the Military
item.description: In a notable shift, Republican senators voted unanimously against a proposal to expand the military’s coverage of fertility treatments.
item.dc:creator: Annie Karni
item.category: United States Defense and Military Forces
item.media:description: Senator Tammy Duckworth, Democrat of Illinois, offered the provision for the defense bill that would have broadened the availability of in vitro fertilization for members of the military.
